learning_outcomes.text: Analyse guided electromagnetic wave propagation in transmission lines, waveguides and optical fibres using analytical and numerical methods.
Understand how the capacity of a communication system is limited by dispersion and attenuation
Analyse electromagnetic wave wireless propagation for realistic scenarios
Apply numerical and analytical models for antenna analysis.
Apply the acquired concepts in the planning of a communication system

syllabus_topics: Pulse propagation in lossy and dispersive transmission lines
Introduction to the design and analysis of antennas
Reflection and dispersion in the ground
assessment_rules: The practical component has a 40% weight with a minimum grade of 9.5 and can be either four laboratory experiences (10%+10%+10%+10%) or an individual project (40%). The written component has a 60% weight and a minimum grade of 9.5 (or 8 if the student attends more than 75% of classes), and can be either two frequencies (30%+30%) or a global written test during the exams season (60%).
bibliography: Barclay L.W., Propagation of Radiowaves, 3rd Edition, IET, 2012.
Engineering Electromagnetics, Kenneth R. Demarest, Prentice-Hall.
Maria João Martins e Isabel Ventim Neves, Propagação e Radiação de Ondas Eletromagnéticas, Lidel, 2015.
Orfanidis, S.J. (2013) Electromagnetic Waves and Antennas. Rutgers University.
